name: Horne-Horowitz Charged Black String in Three Dimensions
description: A straight black string in three spacetime dimensions carrying an axion charge, an exact solution of string theory built from a gauged Wess-Zumino-Witten model. Like the charged black hole of Reissner and Nordström it has an event horizon, an inner horizon, and a timelike singularity, and with no charge it is Witten's black hole of two dimensions times a line.

history: James H. Horne began the construction of this string at the Aspen Center for Physics, and he and Gary T. Horowitz wrote it up at the University of California, Santa Barbara, in a preprint dated July 1991 [horne1992black]. Edward Witten had just found a black hole in two dimensions in the Wess-Zumino-Witten model on the group $SL(2,\mathbb{R})$ with a one dimensional subgroup gauged [witten1991]. Horne and Horowitz added a free boson $x$ to his model and gauged the same subgroup together with a translation of $x$, and the result is an exact conformal field theory of a straight, static string inside an event horizon [horne1992black]. The string carries a mass $M$ and an axion charge $Q$ per unit length, and its string metric is $$ds^2 = -\left(1 - \frac{M}{r}\right)dt^2 + \left(1 - \frac{Q^2}{Mr}\right)dx^2 + \left(1 - \frac{M}{r}\right)^{-1}\left(1 - \frac{Q^2}{Mr}\right)^{-1}\frac{k\,dr^2}{8r^2},$$ with an antisymmetric tensor field $H_{rtx} = Q/r^2$ and a dilaton $\Phi = \ln r + \tfrac{1}{2}\ln(k/2)$ [horne1992black].¶The static charged black holes of string theory with a dilaton have no inner horizon, and their singularity is spacelike, as the Schwarzschild singularity is [horne1992black]. This string, in Horne and Horowitz's words, "has a regular inner horizon (in addition to the event horizon) and a timelike singularity" [horne1992black]. The event horizon is at $r = M$ and the inner horizon at $r = Q^2/M$, and the causal structure follows that of the charged black hole of Hans Reissner and Gunnar Nordström, region by region [horne1992black]. In the Reissner-Nordström hole the Killing vector that translates time far away is timelike again inside the inner horizon; here $\partial_t$ stays spacelike all the way to the singularity, and $\partial_x$, the translation along the string, is timelike inside the inner horizon [horne1992black]. Each point of Horne and Horowitz's diagram is therefore a line along $x$ outside the inner horizon and a line along $t$ inside it [horne1992black]. Timelike geodesics turn back before $r = 0$, so no freely falling observer reaches the singularity, and a light ray with momentum $P$ along the string and energy $E$ reaches it only when $P^2M^2 > E^2Q^2$ [horne1992black].¶With no charge the field $H$ vanishes and the string is Witten's black hole times a line [horne1992black, witten1991]. The Hawking temperature, $T = \sqrt{(M^2 - Q^2)/2k}\,/\pi M$, falls to zero as $|Q|$ approaches $M$, and in that limit, in Horne and Horowitz's words, "the event horizon remains but the singularity disappears" [horne1992black]. At $|Q| = M$ the coordinate $\rho$, with $\rho^2 = r - M$, runs through the horizon from positive to negative values into a copy of the region outside, and observers who cross it, "fortunately for them", find themselves in a second asymptotically flat region identical to the first [horne1992black]. With $r$, $t$, and $x$ rescaled as $|Q|$ goes to $M$, the limit is anti-de Sitter space of three dimensions with a constant dilaton, the ungauged model on $SL(2,\mathbb{R})$ [horne1992black]. For $|Q| > M$ there is neither a horizon nor a curvature singularity, and identifying $x$ with period $\pi|Q|\sqrt{2k/(Q^2 - M^2)}$ removes a conical singularity at the centre and makes each slice of constant $t$ an infinite cigar [horne1992black].¶The constant $k$ is the level of the gauged model, whose central charge, $3k/(k - 2)$, is one more than that of Witten's black hole for the added boson [horne1992black, horowitz1993]. In the low energy equations $k$ appears as a cosmological constant $8/k$, present because that central charge differs from the dimension of spacetime, and only the dilaton's equation carries it, so the equation for the metric holds at every $k$ [horne1992black, horowitz1993]. A bosonic string needs a total central charge of 26, so $k = 52/23$ for this string alone, the value Horowitz and Dean L. Welch gave in 1993 for the same central charge, and a larger $k$ leaves room for an internal conformal field theory beside it [horne1992black, horowitz1993]. The metric is the lowest order in $1/k$, and Konstadinos Sfetsos computed the metric and dilaton of the same model to all orders in 1992, finding a second curvature singularity at finite $k$ that merges with the one at $r = 0$ as $k$ grows without bound [sfetsos1993exact]. Rescaled by the dilaton to the metric of Einstein's action, the string keeps its horizons and is asymptotically flat, but the symmetry that is timelike outside the horizon approaches a boost at infinity, so in that frame the string is not static [horne1992black].¶Horne, Horowitz, and Alan R. Steif showed later in 1991 that the duality of string theory along a direction of translation exchanges the momentum in that direction with the axion charge [horne1992momentum]. The uncharged string of mass $M_0$, boosted along $x$ with rapidity $\alpha$ and then dualized, becomes the charged string with $M = M_0\cosh^2\alpha$ and $Q = M_0\cosh\alpha\sinh\alpha$, so when $x$ is a circle the charged string is equivalent to a boosted uncharged one, which has a spacelike singularity and no inner horizon [horne1992momentum]. Inner horizons in general relativity are unstable, and they argued from that equivalence that the exact solution has no inner horizon, though its low energy metric does [horne1992momentum]. In 1993 Horowitz and Welch made the rotating black hole of Máximo Bañados, Claudio Teitelboim, and Jorge Zanelli an exact solution of string theory and dualized it along its angle into this string, whose charge is half the hole's angular momentum and whose horizons sit where the hole's do [banados1992, horowitz1993]. The hole is asymptotically anti-de Sitter and the string asymptotically flat, which suggested to them that "strings are not affected by a negative cosmological constant in three dimensions" [horowitz1993].¶Roberto Emparan, Daniel Grumiller, and Kentaro Tanabe found this string in 2013 as the geometry near the horizon of black branes with an electric string charge and no dilaton, in the limit of a large number of dimensions [emparan2013strings]. Luis Apolo, Stéphane Detournay, and Wei Song reached it in 2020 from the black hole of Bañados, Teitelboim, and Zanelli through a duality, a shift, and a second duality, and identified the string of fixed charge as the dual of a thermal state of a conformal field theory deformed by $T\bar{T}$ [apolo2020black]. Jeongwon Ho, Wontae Kim, and Bum-Hoon Lee followed massive scalar waves to the inner horizon in 2022, and found strong cosmic censorship respected far from extremality and violated near it for a heavy enough field, so that it "can be violated even for an asymptotically flat spacetime" [ho2022strong].

related.text: Witten's black hole of two dimensions, the cross section of this string when it carries no charge. Horne and Horowitz built the charged string by adding a line to Witten's model and gauging a translation along it [horne1992black].

The charged black hole of general relativity, with the same diagram of horizons and singularity. Inside its inner horizon the time translation is timelike again, and here the translation along the string takes that role [horne1992black].

The rotating black hole of three dimensions with a negative cosmological constant. Dualized along its angle it becomes this string, its angular momentum turned into twice the string's charge and its horizons left where they were [horowitz1993].

Schwarzschild's black hole stretched along a line, a static black string of general relativity, which needs five dimensions or more when matter obeys the strong energy condition [horne1992black, horowitz1991]. This one lives in three, where the dilaton and antisymmetric field of its string metric violate that condition [horne1992black].
The charged black hole of string theory in four dimensions, with one horizon and no inner horizon for every charge. Its singularity is spacelike, and the string's is timelike [horne1992black].

In the limit $|Q| \to M$ with $r$, $t$, and $x$ rescaled, the string becomes anti-de Sitter space of three dimensions with a constant dilaton, the ungauged model on $SL(2,\mathbb{R})$ [horne1992black].

coordinates.name: Static

parameters.description: Mass per unit length of the string
Axion charge per unit length of the string
Level of the gauged Wess-Zumino-Witten model, $k = 52/23$ for the string alone

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, x, r)$, with $x$ along the string and $r$ fixed by the dilaton, $\Phi = \ln r + \tfrac{1}{2}\ln(k/2)$.
geodesics: \ddot{r} - \dfrac{4\left(M - r\right)\left(M\,r - Q^2\right)}{k\,r^2}\dot{t}^2 + \dfrac{4Q^2\left(M - r\right)\left(M\,r - Q^2\right)}{M^2\,k\,r^2}\dot{x}^2 - \dfrac{M^2 - 2M\,r + Q^2}{2\left(M - r\right)\left(M\,r - Q^2\right)}\dot{r}^2 = 0

coordinates.name: Wess-Zumino-Witten

parameters.description: Mass per unit length of the string
Axion charge per unit length of the string
Level of the gauged Wess-Zumino-Witten model, $k = 52/23$ for the string alone

coordinates.convention: We use the coordinates $(u, v)$ of $SL(2,\mathbb{R})$ in which the model is gauged, with $r = M - (M^2 - Q^2)uv/M$ and, outside the event horizon, $u/v = -e^{2\kappa t}$, $\kappa = \sqrt{2(M^2 - Q^2)/k}/M$.
coordinates.line_element: ds^2 = -\dfrac{k\left(Q^2v^2\,du^2 + Q^2u^2\,dv^2 + 2\left(2M^2 - (2M^2 - Q^2)uv\right)du\,dv\right)}{8(1 - uv)\left(M^2 - (M^2 - Q^2)uv\right)} + \dfrac{(M^2 - Q^2)(1 - uv)}{M^2 - (M^2 - Q^2)uv}\,dx^2

nonzero.value: -\dfrac{2Q^2\left(u\,v - 1\right)\left(M + Q\right)\left(M - Q\right)\left(M^2\,u\,v + M^2 - Q^2\,u\,v\right)}{k\left(M^2\,u\,v - M^2 - Q^2\,u\,v\right)^3}
\dfrac{2Q^2\left(u\,v - 1\right)\left(M + Q\right)\left(M - Q\right)\left(M^2\,u\,v + M^2 - Q^2\,u\,v\right)}{k\left(M^2\,u\,v - M^2 - Q^2\,u\,v\right)^3}
-\dfrac{2Q^2\left(u\,v - 1\right)\left(M + Q\right)\left(M - Q\right)\left(M^2\,u\,v + M^2 - Q^2\,u\,v\right)}{k\left(M^2\,u\,v - M^2 - Q^2\,u\,v\right)^3}
\dfrac{2Q^2\left(u\,v - 1\right)\left(M + Q\right)\left(M - Q\right)\left(M^2\,u\,v + M^2 - Q^2\,u\,v\right)}{k\left(M^2\,u\,v - M^2 - Q^2\,u\,v\right)^3}
-\dfrac{4Q^2\left(u\,v - 1\right)\left(M + Q\right)\left(M - Q\right)\left(M^2\,u\,v + M^2 - Q^2\,u\,v\right)}{k\left(M^2\,u\,v - M^2 - Q^2\,u\,v\right)^3}
\dfrac{4Q^2\left(Q^2\,u\,v - M^2 - M^2\,u\,v\right)}{k\left(u\,v - 1\right)\left(M + Q\right)\left(M - Q\right)\left(M^2\,u\,v - M^2 - Q^2\,u\,v\right)}

geodesics: \ddot{u} + \dfrac{v\left(3Q^4\,u\,v - 4Q^4\,u^2\,v^2 + 4M^2\,Q^2 - 12M^2\,Q^2\,u\,v + 8M^2\,Q^2\,u^2\,v^2 - 4M^4 + 8M^4\,u\,v - 4M^4\,u^2\,v^2\right)}{4\left(u\,v - 1\right)\left(M^2\,u\,v - M^2 - Q^2\,u\,v\right)^2}\dot{u}^2 + \dfrac{Q^2\,u\left(2M^2\,u\,v - 2M^2 - Q^2\,u\,v\right)}{2\left(u\,v - 1\right)\left(M^2\,u\,v - M^2 - Q^2\,u\,v\right)^2}\dot{u}\dot{v} - \dfrac{Q^4\,u^3}{4\left(u\,v - 1\right)\left(M^2\,u\,v - M^2 - Q^2\,u\,v\right)^2}\dot{v}^2 + \dfrac{2Q^2\,u\left(u\,v - 1\right)\left(M + Q\right)\left(M - Q\right)}{k\left(M^2\,u\,v - M^2 - Q^2\,u\,v\right)^2}\dot{x}^2 = 0

\ddot{v} - \dfrac{Q^4\,v^3}{4\left(u\,v - 1\right)\left(M^2\,u\,v - M^2 - Q^2\,u\,v\right)^2}\dot{u}^2 + \dfrac{Q^2\,v\left(2M^2\,u\,v - 2M^2 - Q^2\,u\,v\right)}{2\left(u\,v - 1\right)\left(M^2\,u\,v - M^2 - Q^2\,u\,v\right)^2}\dot{u}\dot{v} + \dfrac{u\left(3Q^4\,u\,v - 4Q^4\,u^2\,v^2 + 4M^2\,Q^2 - 12M^2\,Q^2\,u\,v + 8M^2\,Q^2\,u^2\,v^2 - 4M^4 + 8M^4\,u\,v - 4M^4\,u^2\,v^2\right)}{4\left(u\,v - 1\right)\left(M^2\,u\,v - M^2 - Q^2\,u\,v\right)^2}\dot{v}^2 + \dfrac{2Q^2\,v\left(u\,v - 1\right)\left(M + Q\right)\left(M - Q\right)}{k\left(M^2\,u\,v - M^2 - Q^2\,u\,v\right)^2}\dot{x}^2 = 0

coordinates.name: Ingoing Eddington-Finkelstein

parameters.description: Mass per unit length of the string
Axion charge per unit length of the string
Level of the gauged Wess-Zumino-Witten model, $k = 52/23$ for the string alone

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(v, x, r)$, with the advanced time $dv = dt + \sqrt{k/8}\,dr/\left(r(1 - M/r)\sqrt{1 - Q^2/(Mr)}\right)$.
geodesics: \ddot{r} - \dfrac{4\left(M - r\right)\left(M\,r - Q^2\right)}{k\,r^2}\dot{v}^2 - \dfrac{2\sqrt{2}\sqrt{M}\sqrt{M\,r - Q^2}}{\sqrt{k}\,r^{3/2}}\dot{v}\dot{r} + \dfrac{4Q^2\left(M - r\right)\left(M\,r - Q^2\right)}{M^2\,k\,r^2}\dot{x}^2 + \dfrac{Q^2 - 2M\,r}{2r\left(M\,r - Q^2\right)}\dot{r}^2 = 0

parameters.description: Mass per unit length of the string
Level of the gauged Wess-Zumino-Witten model, $k = 52/23$ for the string alone

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, x, \rho)$ at $|Q| = M$, with $\rho^2 = r - M$.

parameters.description: Mass per unit length of the string
Level of the gauged Wess-Zumino-Witten model, $k = 52/23$ for the string alone

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, x, \rho)$ inside the horizon at $|Q| = M$, with $\rho^2 = M - r$.

coordinates.name: Superextremal

parameters.description: Mass per unit length of the string
Axion charge per unit length of the string
Level of the gauged Wess-Zumino-Witten model, $k = 52/23$ for the string alone

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, x, \rho)$ at $|Q| > M$, with $\rho^2 = r - Q^2/M$ and $x$ of period $\pi|Q|\sqrt{2k/(Q^2 - M^2)}$.
coordinates.line_element: ds^2 = -\dfrac{Q^2 - M^2 + M\rho^2}{Q^2 + M\rho^2}dt^2 + \dfrac{M\rho^2}{Q^2 + M\rho^2}dx^2 + \dfrac{Mk\,d\rho^2}{2\left(Q^2 - M^2 + M\rho^2\right)}
geodesics: \ddot{\rho} + \dfrac{2M^2\,\rho\left(Q^2 + M\,\rho^2 - M^2\right)}{k\left(M\,\rho^2 + Q^2\right)^2}\dot{t}^2 + \dfrac{2Q^2\,\rho\left(M^2 - M\,\rho^2 - Q^2\right)}{k\left(M\,\rho^2 + Q^2\right)^2}\dot{x}^2 + \dfrac{M\,\rho}{M^2 - M\,\rho^2 - Q^2}\dot{\rho}^2 = 0
